title: 2022 AMC 12A Problem 6
statement: A data set consists of \(6\) (not distinct) positive integers: \(1,\) \(7,\) \(5,\) \(2,\) \(5,\) and \(X.\) The average (arithmetic mean) of the \(6\) numbers equals a value in the data set. What is the sum of all positive values of \(X?\)

solutions.text:
The known numbers sum to \(20,\) so the mean is \(\dfrac{20+X}{6},\) which must equal an element of the set.

Setting it to \(5\) gives \(X=10;\) to \(7\) gives \(X=22;\) and to \(X\) itself gives \(20+X=6X,\) so \(X=4.\) Values \(1\) and \(2\) give negative \(X.\)

The positive values are \(10,22,4,\) summing to \(36.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The five known numbers sum to \(20,\) so the mean is \(\dfrac{20+X}{6}\)
The mean must equal one of \(1,2,5,7,\) or \(X;\) only some give positive \(X\)
